question: Choose the figure that is different from the others (odd man out).
options: <svg xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg" viewBox="0 0 100 100"><rect width="100" height="100" fill="#fff"/><polygon points="28.6,27.7 71.4,27.7 71.4,72.3 28.6,72.3" fill="none" stroke="#111" stroke-width="2.5" stroke-linejoin="round"/></svg>

<svg xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg" viewBox="0 0 100 100"><rect width="100" height="100" fill="#fff"/><polygon points="19,72.3 38.1,27.7 59.1,27.7 81,72.3" fill="none" stroke="#111" stroke-width="2.5" stroke-linejoin="round"/></svg>

<svg xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg" viewBox="0 0 100 100"><rect width="100" height="100" fill="#fff"/><polygon points="28,50.3 28,84.5 72,57.3 72,15.5" fill="none" stroke="#111" stroke-width="2.5" stroke-linejoin="round"/></svg>
<svg xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg" viewBox="0 0 100 100"><rect width="100" height="100" fill="#fff"/><circle cx="50" cy="50" r="22" fill="none" stroke="#111" stroke-width="2.5"/></svg>
why: Options 1-4 are all four-sided shapes with straight sides (square, parallelogram, trapezium, parallelogram). Option 5 is a circle, with no straight sides and no corners.
trick: Count sides and corners first; a curved shape is often the odd one among polygons.
